390.title: The Vegan Events Guide - Vegans Explore Guides
h2: The day itself
What to do when it rains
h3: GUESTS WHO SAID YES AND DO NOT COME
A VENDOR WHO DOES NOT COME
items: Say it on the listing from day one: rain or shine, or a rain date. Put the same words in your refund policy.
Set your rain call time in advance, the day before and again that morning, and tell vendors and guests when it is.
Line up a covered fallback while you plan: a pavilion, a restaurant's room, a garage, an indoor partner.
Weight every leg of every canopy, and take canopies down when the wind picks up. Ask your venue how much weight they want per leg.
Sidewalls on the side the weather comes from, tarps under the tables, lidded tubs for paper goods, zip bags for card readers, towels.
Keep cords and connections off the ground and covered, and plug into outdoor outlets that cut off if they get wet.
If you hear thunder, everyone goes inside: lightning can strike miles from the storm. Wait until thunder has stopped for 30 minutes before g
Shade for guests and vendors, and free water for everyone, refilled all day.
Hold the outdoor parts in the cooler hours, and keep a cool spot where people can sit down.
Ice for food vendors, and somewhere for them to keep it.
Know the signs of heat illness, and who on your team handles first aid.
GUESTS WHO SAID YES AND DO NOT COME
Send a reminder two days before and the morning of, and ask anyone who cannot come to give their spot back.
Keep a waitlist, and fill spots from it.
A small price, or a deposit back at the door, brings the people who mean it.
Plan the food and the room for the people who come, not the RSVP count.
A VENDOR WHO DOES NOT COME
Confirm every vendor in writing three days before.
Keep a short standby list of vendors who would come at short notice.
Never leave a gap by the entrance: move a table, spread the row, put your own table there.
Say in your vendor agreement what happens to a fee when a vendor does not come.
Charge every card reader, phone and power bank the night before, and know your card reader's offline mode.
Battery lanterns and a battery speaker, so the room is never dark or silent.
If you run a generator, keep it outside and far from tents, doors and windows: its exhaust can kill.
Know who at the venue resets the breakers.

links.text: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, Heat and Health
Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, Carbon Monoxide Poisoning
